prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape approximately 3:2, plain light background, crisp voxel style, vanilla Minecraft blocks only, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT straight-on front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT three-quarter front-right view at the same block scale. Show the same complete building in both views with clear separation and margins. Skilled human builder quality: real massing and depth, projecting counters and upper storey, recessed framed openings, real roof verges, eaves and ridge, stairs/slabs/fences/walls/trapdoors/lantern details. No invented curved architectural components.
Site: traditional German town bakery seen from a gravel lane, tall gable end facing street. Ground storey charcoal deepslate brick on smooth darker plinth. Centred spruce front door with glass transom between two wide three-pane shop windows. Each has projecting spruce-slab sales counter and folded-back spruce shutters. Tan stripped-spruce lintel beam across entire front; exactly five spruce brackets support upper storey projecting one block over pavement. Upper storey classic Fachwerk: stripped-spruce posts, sill/head beams and breast rail; bright white panels; darker spruce stair diagonal braces in end panels. Two 2x2 windows with red-tulip flower boxes. Steep grey slate roof, dark tiles with lighter mottling, spruce barge boards, high ridge running back from street. Timbered front gable with collar beam, king post, two small attic windows and open central loft door with shutters. Above loft door stripped-spruce hoist beam projects beyond verge, iron chain suspends barrel. Wrought-style hanging sign made from vanilla sign and chain, reading exactly "Bäckerei", on spruce arm at right corner; lanterns under overhang.
Set back on right: lower single-storey cobbled-deepslate bakehouse wing with its own small slate gable. At back red-brick bread oven projects into yard with stepped brick stair/slab barrel-vault approximation. Slim brick chimney with dark band and campfire smoke rises to height 17, about two-thirds main roof height. Behind house spruce-fenced yard with stacked spruce firewood, barrels, hay bales, small wheat patch and exactly two small spruce trees. Arrange right view to expose rear-yard features as far as physical occlusion allows.
Dimensions in Minecraft blocks: site 24 wide x 32 deep; main house 11 wide x 15 deep; bakehouse wing 5 wide plus oven; two storeys and steep attic; main ridge 21 high; chimney 17 high.

changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved without post-processing as concept.png.

Block identities are visual interpretations, not a recoverable Minecraft block inventory. The roles retain every planned block; additions describe the closest vanilla equivalents. Campfire is inferred from oven fire and chimney smoke; flower pots are mostly concealed.
Both shop windows have roughly three columns and two rows of panes instead of a single three-pane arrangement.
The whole-front lintel is fragmented by individual wooden window headers and stone sections.
The upper-storey breast rail is not clearly expressed as a continuous separate beam.
The render does not establish an exact one-block overhang or reliably countable block dimensions; the 24x32 site, 11x15 house, five-wide wing and specified heights cannot be verified.
The roof textures resemble deepslate bricks more than distinct deepslate tiles; the lighter mottling and polished-blackstone eave band are not clearly differentiated.
The ridge looks like a full-height masonry cap rather than exclusively deepslate_brick_slab.
The bakehouse wing sits close to the front corner and its doorway faces the street.
The oven is a large stepped brick structure with a curved-looking arched mouth; its barrel-vaulted top is not distinctly represented.
The chimney is comparatively thick and reaches nearly the main ridge height rather than about two-thirds of it.
The fenced wheat patch and storage yard extend along the right side toward the street rather than remaining behind the house.
Extra barrels stand beside the wing at the front.
The flower boxes contain three tulips each, but individual vanilla pots cannot be resolved.
Bread-like piles appear on the shop counters and loft sill. These are invented decorative forms with no exact vanilla placeable-block id.
The hanging barrel has rounded detailing, and several textures and small fittings are stylized beyond strict vanilla block geometry.
The right view presents the building slightly smaller vertically than the left, so the requested identical scale is approximate.
